catalog.summary: Start and end date-times with a picker.

valueRules.empty: a request whose both ends are null carries null; the family speaks one word for nothing
valueRules.openEnd: { start, end: null } and { start: null, end } are values: an open end is written in the field, where the reader sees it
valueRules.reversed: an end typed before its start is invalid and stays as typed
valueRules.halves: a PlainDateTime is whole or it is nothing: a date without a time, or a time without a date, lives in the draft while the panel is open, never in the value

pattern.title: Date Picker Dialog Example, for the popup; Grid Pattern, for the months, which calendar draws; Listbox Pattern, for the grids of the clocks, which clock draws
pattern.rangePattern: none exists; the dialog example for the popup, and the patterns the composed families transcribe
pattern.departure: the dialog example closes on the first press and this family closes on Apply, because a range with hours is at least four presses; confirm=false names the rest

panel.shape: a rail of shortcuts, lengths and months, the two ends and the length between them, the months, and a clock for each end
panel.halves: a datetime field in each at 760 px and above, while the end is whole or empty; the day and the time in words, as two presses, while one of them is missing and below 760 px
panel.months: two by default, over two clocks of the same module
panel.clocks: one for each end, under its half; below 760 px the one of the end being edited
panel.why: One end at a time hid the other behind a tab, and a list of times showed nine in a hundred of them. The run is drawn over its months, both ends are written, and a time is two presses.

focusRule.rule: the press that leaves a half missing carries focus to its grid: the clock of the end whose day was pressed, then the months for the other end, then its clock
focusRule.open: the chosen day of the current end, or today
focusRule.whole: with nothing missing, focus stays where the reader put it

draft.rule: a press, a typed end, a step, a length and a shortcut write a draft; Apply writes the value with reason select
draft.halves: each end of the draft holds its date and time as two nullable halves, so a chosen day waits for its time and a chosen time waits for its day
draft.abandonedBy: Escape, an outside press and the trigger abandon the draft and keep the previous value
draft.confirm: false writes a whole run on every change the rules take, and closes on the press that completes it

length.between: the two halves of the head, with a step of one day of the end either way
length.pending: the run as it would close on the pending day, with the time each end already holds
length.incomplete: while a time is missing, the days between the two ends
length.unit: seconds between the two ends, turned into words
length.label: durationLabel(seconds, locale, granularity) by default, replaceable per instance and per provider as lengthLabel(seconds, locale)

position.meaning: the end whose half and clock carry data-current, the end the next press in the grid writes, and the one clock a narrow panel shows

calendarReceives.end: { start, end: null }, so the next press writes the end instead of restarting the run
calendarReceives.start: the whole value, so the next press restarts the run

position.calendarOrders: when the grid orders the two dates — an end pressed before the start — the hours stay with the end they were on
position.afterMissing: the end whose half is missing
position.afterHalf: the half that was pressed or focused

step.base: min's time when min is stated, midnight when it is not
step.notTheFieldArrows: the panel's step is the panel's; a segment steps by one of its own unit

limits.dayWindow: each clock runs between dayWindow(date, { min, max, minTime, maxTime }) for the day of its end
limits.crossed: on the day of the start, the clock of the end starts after it

contiguous.grid: with an open run, the days beyond the first unavailable day after the start are refused in the grid, through blockedAround as date-range-picker
contiguous.clock: on the same day, the times past the first unavailable one after the start are refused in the clock of the end
contiguous.search: once per chosen start over the days, up to 366; over the offered times for the same day
contiguous.typed: the day predicate runs over every day between two typed ends and the time predicate over the two ends, once per value change

limits.explained: the footer names minLength and maxLength while either is set, and the stated zone otherwise; over them, it says by how much and the days past the limit carry data-over

validity.owned: bounds, the day window, unavailable days and times, the order of the two ends, and the duration
validity.reversed: an end before its start is invalid on the end field and on the frame; the ends are not swapped

clear.fields: the two fields do not draw their own clear; one button on the frame empties both ends with reason clear

wiring.aria-expanded: the trigger, while the popup is showing
wiring.aria-controls: the content, while the popup is showing
wiring.aria-label: the trigger, carrying both ends and the duration

triggerName.chosen: the change message, with both ends in words and the duration in its start, end and length slots; changeReversed, without the duration, while the ends are out of order
triggerName.why: Focus returns to the trigger when the popup closes, so the name is where the reader is told what was chosen.

keyboard.focusTo: the cell of the current end, or today when it is empty
the cell of the current end, or today when it is empty

keyboard.staged: the relative expression of a field, then the calendar's view, then the panel

platformNotes.altArrowDown: ChromeOS turns Alt+ArrowDown into PageDown before the browser sees it, which Angular Material records for its own input. The trigger button is therefore the guaranteed path and the chord is a shortcut, never the only way in.

dismissal.escape: through dismissable-layer, in the capture phase

branches: the trigger, so pressing it again closes rather than dismissing and reopening

responsive.below760: one month, and one part at a time on data-showing: the days, or the clock of the end being edited; the halves are buttons that bring them; the length is not drawn
responsive.sheet: below 480px on a coarse pointer, the content takes the sheet presentation
responsive.decidedIn: the stylesheet, except the months and the halves, whose field would open a keyboard

portalledIdentity.reason: The popup is picker-panel's: its positioner carries that family's data-ui, and the control carries this one's.

forms.angular: ControlValueAccessor writes the whole DateTimeRange; Validator reports the family's own errors
forms.hiddenInputs: two, on the frame, because the panel in a portal is not inside the form while it is closed

dataAttributes.data-granularity: hour, minute or second, on the root
dataAttributes.data-calendar: the calendar axis, on the root
dataAttributes.data-placeholder: on summary: there is no value and the text is the placeholder

control.shape: one line at the control height: the value written short in the locale, or the placeholder, cut with an ellipsis when it does not fit, a clear, and the trigger that fills the frame
control.why: two datetime fields in one frame need about 360 pixels on one line, a segment cannot shrink, and below that the frame broke into two lines against the control height every form counts on. Withdrawn at the visual gate on the reviewer's reading; a container query could not hide the fields without duplicating them in the panel for typing
control.fullName: the trigger carries both ends in words and the duration, so the ellipsis removes nothing a reader cannot hear

closing.clock: on the day of the start, the clock of the end refuses the times up to it, those whose run is too short or too long, and with contiguous those past the first unavailable one; on another day, those outside the limits
closing.grid: with a start open, the days past the first unavailable one, and those no time of which is inside the limits
closing.refusedDrawn: struck and aria-disabled, where it stands

durations.refused: disabled without a whole start, or refused by a rule

presets.result: the two days, the parts they share written once
